races.name: Hadwins Novices' Hurdle Race (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Newbrook Diamond
runners_data.note: Recent course-and-distance winner whose Good-ground record reads 2W2P from eight similar starts; Elliott's 6yo mare is exactly the type to pop from prominent to devastating in the final stages of a moderately run Cartmel novice.

runners_data.name: Rebel Tribesman
runners_data.note: Four from four on Good ground with strong form figures of 1-2-2-1 in that going, but his naturally front-running instincts are squeezed by a crowded prominent division here — how he adapts to racing a length or two further back than ideal will decide his fate.

runners_data.name: Viscountess Nelson
runners_data.note: Henderson-trained 6yo with a recent win on Good and a solid placed record; amateur rider Mr Daniel Williams claiming 7lb is a mild unknown, but the horse's form entitles it to be prominent throughout and it has the class to win this grade.

runners_data.name: Nightflyer
runners_data.note: OR 120 but arrives here having failed to trouble the judge in his last four, including a well-beaten fifth on Good last time; his value today is purely as pace-setter and the STYLE_FIT flag correctly signals that his chance of winning from the front under Jonjo O'Neill Jr. is constrained by modest recent form.

runners_data.name: Frisky Whiskey
runners_data.note: A true hold-up performer on a tongue-tie, running 27 days fresh, with three outings all producing mid-to-rear finishes on Good; Brian Ellison sends him here off OR 120 but the horse is occupying a midfield slot that does not reflect how he actually races, and his form line of 664 is uninspiring.

runners_data.name: Order Another One
runners_data.note: Dianne Sayer's headgear-wearing (hood) 5yo has only one run to his name in similar going — a seventh — and his form string of 344-17 shows a horse that has not threatened at this level; needs a truly searching gallop to have any chance from the rear.

runners_data.name: Manhatane
runners_data.note: James Moffatt's 4yo carries the lowest weight at 142lbs with claimer Leah Noreci (7lb) aboard, and his sole comparable run produced a fifth over further on Good; unproven at this level and likely to need experience rather than deliver a result here.

races.paceDynamic: Nightflyer is the confirmed front-runner and will set a sustainable, uncontested gallop over 2m6f on Good ground at Cartmel — a sharp, undulating track that rewards those who can travel economically and quicken late rather than those who grind from the front. With just one genuine pace-setter, the tempo is unlikely to be fierce, creating a relatively controlled race that will suit prominent and mid-division types who can be delivered with energy in reserve for the final climb. Newbrook Diamond and Viscountess Nelson are the natural prominent horses best placed to capitalise on that shape, sitting just off Nightflyer and pouncing when the race quickens. This race shape most clearly favours the prominent racer who travels smoothly close to a manageable pace and has the class to accelerate — the hold-up horses face the added burden of making ground on a sharp circuit where gaps can close quickly. The field contains more front-running and prominent runners than the pace map can accommodate: Rebel Tribesman is a genuine prominent type forced into a midfield berth, and Frisky Whiskey, a natural hold-up horse, is similarly displaced — Newbrook Diamond and Viscountess Nelson are the horses most likely to actually secure their natural position just behind Nightflyer.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Prominent Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Nightflyer controls a true-to-form moderate gallop and the prominent pair track him throughout.
scenarios.body: Newbrook Diamond and Viscountess Nelson settle beautifully in the slipstream, conserve energy through the back straight, and are best placed to pounce jumping the last; Gordon Elliott's mare arrives on the back of a recent win and handles Good ground convincingly. This is the dominant shape for this race — one uncontested front-runner, a tractable pace, and two class-act prominent types with the credentials to win from that position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Nightflyer Scores Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Nightflyer is allowed to bowl along unchallenged and the pace is so moderate that he simply never gets headed.
scenarios.body: On a sharp Cartmel track with only six rivals and no one willing to pressurise him, Nightflyer could control fractions perfectly and simply not be caught; Jonjo O'Neill Jr. is an astute enough judge to exploit that freedom. Despite the STYLE_FIT flag, the complete absence of pace pressure could make his natural role suddenly viable.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Nightflyer sets a genuinely strong gallop that burns off the prominent horses and leaves a gap for a late finisher.
scenarios.body: Order Another One or Manhatane would need the race to develop into a true stamina test, grinding down tiring rivals over the final two flights; both are hold-up types suited to a stronger pace but carry limited form credentials at this level. The scenario is discounted because there is no secondary pace pressure to force that outcome and the most likely gallop is measured.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistribution Chaos, Upset
scenarios.trigger: If the compressed field causes early jostling that unsettles the prominent horses and hands an advantage to a resettled Rebel Tribesman or Frisky Whiskey.
scenarios.body: Rebel Tribesman has strong Good-ground form and, if traffic issues force a reshuffled order in the early stages, he has the raw ability to recover and hit the line hard; Frisky Whiskey on a tongue-tie and 27 days fresh is an unknown quantity but capable of outrunning his modest recent figures. Both horses are racing partially out of role, so this is a low-probability but non-trivial upset route.

watchPoints.text: Rebel Tribesman forced into a midfield berth despite being a natural front-runner — watch for early crowding if he tries to push forward and how Gavin Sheehan handles the compromised position in the first half-mile.

Viscountess Nelson ridden by a 7lb claimer in Mr Daniel Williams — watch for any positional error jumping the early hurdles that could disrupt her natural prominent role against more experienced handlers.

Nightflyer's gallop tempo is the race's pivotal variable — if Jonjo O'Neill Jr. allows him to bowl along at a genuinely steady pace, the prominent pair may never have to work, but any injection of pace in the back straight changes the entire complexion.

Order Another One and Manhatane are both hold-up types with thin form lines — watch whether either is given a confidence-building ride rather than being asked a serious question, which would further reduce their impact on the finish.

Good ground is confirmed across all seven races at Cartmel today; no going concern for any runner, but watch the draw/starting positions given Cartmel's compact, turning nature and the potential for early bunching with seven runners.

races.name: Cartmel Novices' Limited Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Mr Lincoln
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with solid Good-ground placed form (3W at sim-going, 0 wins but consistent); Sean Quinlan and Iain Jardine have strong 14-day figures (6/33) and the 14-day freshen-up suits — likely to track from deep and challenge late if the race is truly run to suit closers.

runners_data.name: Made All
runners_data.note: Trainer Sam England and Jonathan England partnership with a tidy 1/6 T14 strike rate; holds five placed efforts in five recent runs on Good ground and returns just three days after a run, which risks a short-turnaround blip, but the consistent placings suggest reliability rather than a horse crying out for a break.

runners_data.name: Animato
runners_data.note: Donald McCain's runner carries tongue-strap and pads, and while a genuine hold-up horse by nature, is shown in midfield because the rear is oversubscribed — the 14-day freshen-up counts in its favour and three recent placed efforts at up to 17f suggests it stays this trip well, though the compromised position is a real tactical handicap.

runners_data.name: Daring To Dream
runners_data.note: Harriet Dickin yard is cold at T14 (0/3) and this 5-year-old has struggled for consistency lately (form: 4736-8), making it hard to be positive; a true hold-up type squeezed into midfield on the map, its recent Good-ground record (4/8 sim-going, 0 wins) points to modest rather than exciting claims here.

runners_data.name: King Kodiak
runners_data.note: George Bewley's 7-year-old wears tongue-strap and cheekpieces and is naturally a hold-up horse shifted to midfield given the crowded tail of this field; the 2/16f Good run in recent history is the one standout moment but the yard has an inactive fortnight (T14: 0/0) and the overall profile lacks the consistency to inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Alvesta
runners_data.note: The only winner in the field (1W from recent runs), scored over 17f on Good ground last time out with Brian Hughes aboard — a strong trainer-jockey combo in theory, though Moffatt's T14 is quiet (0/0); a natural hold-up horse repositioned to midfield, but Alvesta's jumping ability and proven winning form on this going make it the most interesting of the redistributed group.

runners_data.name: Ribble River
runners_data.note: Lizzie Quinlan's 5-year-old is the race's sole confirmed front-runner and will lead from flag to finish; the tongue-tie is a notable addition and the 35-day break gives McMenamin a fresh horse to dictate on, but OR=76 is lowest in the field and the ability ceiling may be exposed if the better-rated hold-up types get a clean run at the last.

runners_data.name: Mr Globalist
runners_data.note: Consistent Good-ground performer (14/15 sim-going entries on Good, 0 wins but placed twice) whose headgear (visor) has not unlocked a win yet; Harry Atkins (5lb claimer) takes off the weight burden but the Quinlan yard is inactive at T14 (0/0), and as a hold-up horse mapped to midfield, Mr Globalist needs things to go smoothly to capitalise on any late opening.

races.paceDynamic: Ribble River is the sole confirmed pace-setter and will stride to the front unchallenged from the off, setting a sustainable gallop around Cartmel's tight, idiosyncratic circuit over 2m1f on Good ground. With no other genuine front-runner in the field, the pace is unlikely to be pressured at any stage, meaning the race will be run at a steady, controlled tempo dictated entirely by Danny McMenamin aboard the lowest-rated runner in the field. This race shape — a lone leader going an honest but not suicidal gallop — classically suits hold-up horses with a strong late kick, provided the race doesn't collapse into a falsely slow crawl that turns it into a sprint and renders the hold-up approach void. The field holds significantly more hold-up types than can realistically occupy deep rearward positions; Animato, Daring To Dream, King Kodiak, Alvesta and Mr Globalist are all true hold-up horses redistributed into midfield on the map, meaning the genuine finishing positions will be bunched and competitive, and those with the cleaner jumps and straightforward finishes from mid-division are best placed to exploit the pace shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace Suits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Ribble River leads at a controlled gallop and the field tracks comfortably in a tight group before a straight-line sprint develops.
scenarios.body: Ribble River's uncontested front-running tempo will be sustainable but not fast enough to string out the field, compressing the race into a finish where the best-credentialed hold-up types landing from mid-division will have first run; Made All and Mr Lincoln, both going ok on Good ground with consistent placed form, are best positioned to pick off the leader entering the home straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If the steady pace proves deceptively honest and Ribble River's jumping accuracy and fitness allow it to hold on as the hold-up pack fails to close.
scenarios.body: Ribble River's tongue-tie and a notably fresh 35-day break could mean McMenamin has the horse primed to jump fluently and steal enough of a cushion rounding the final bend that the muddled midfield pack cannot coordinate a challenge; the lowest-rated runner in the field winning would be a shock but is the logical consequence of no pace pressure.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Surprise Prominent Racer Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses into a falsely slow slog and one of the redistributed hold-up horses breaks forward early to claim a prominent berth.
scenarios.body: Animato (tongue-strap, 14-day turnaround, Donald McCain in decent form at T14) or Alvesta (the only winner in the field, winning last time on Good at 17f) could push forward and find themselves closer to the pace than their natural style dictates, benefiting if rivals lack the acceleration to quicken.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors disrupt the tempo or a mid-race incident forces a reshuffle that breaks the field into isolated groups.
scenarios.body: With eight novice-limited handicappers over Cartmel's unique circuit — including hurdlers wearing headgear such as King Kodiak (tongue-strap/pads) and Made All (headgear noted) — a jumping mistake at a key hurdle could fragment the race and produce a winner from a completely unexpected position; Mr Globalist, consistent on Good but yet to win, could scramble home in a messy finish.

watchPoints.text: Ribble River sets the pace entirely alone — watch whether McMenamin attempts to steal an unassailable lead or sits quietly, as the choice will dictate whether hold-up horses can close or are left chasing shadows.

Made All runs just three days after its previous outing — monitor for any sign of fatigue or below-par jumping, as a short-turnaround horse tracking the pace could unravel quickly if it fails to travel with the same fluency as recent runs.

Alvesta is the lone proven winner in this field and Brian Hughes knows the horse — watch for it making an unexpectedly forward move into contention given how cramped the midfield will be with five true hold-up types jostling for the same real estate.

With Animato, Daring To Dream, King Kodiak, Alvesta and Mr Globalist all naturally wanting to race from the back but mapped into midfield, watch for early positional jostling as riders fight for the cleanest routes — any crowding or poor jumps in the early stages could compromise multiple fancies simultaneously.

King Kodiak's cheekpieces and tongue-strap combination and a yard with zero runners in 14 days (T14: 0/0) are worth monitoring in the paddock — if the horse is unsettled or not jumping fluently in the early exchanges, its chances in an already compromised tactical position will evaporate quickly.

races.name: RF Miller & Co Female Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle Race (Female Professional Jockeys And Amateur Riders' Race)

runners_data.name: My Chiquita
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner here at OR 125 with an excellent recent record in similar Good-ground hurdles — 13 from 15 in comparable conditions — and should slot in just behind Eternal Angel from her prominent style, giving Leah Noreci (7) a strong platform; 56 days off is not a concern given the yard's record at this level.

runners_data.name: Saligo Bay
runners_data.note: Has won three of her last five starts at OR 123 and clearly appreciates Good ground, though all five recent runs were on softer; Miss Heidi Palin takes 5lb and this is 168 days since a run, so fitness is the key question mark against genuine class claims.

runners_data.name: Percy Shelley
runners_data.note: Prolific Good-ground performer with 14 from 15 runs on similar going and a recent second over this trip, making him a solid each-way profile; the visor is on and James Owen's stable is in good form at 8/48 over 14 days, suggesting the horse is being trained up to a peak.

runners_data.name: Eternal Angel
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner who will lead from the off on ground she handles well — her two wins this season have both come on Good, and 11 days' turnaround for the Tom Lacey yard (1/5 in 14 days) is comfortable; the key question is whether the prominent pack behind her exerts enough pressure to find her out late.

runners_data.name: Secret Force
runners_data.note: A four-year-old prominent racer who ran just seven days ago, which may leave a fitness question mark at this stage of his development; Good-ground form is limited at 6 from 12, and stepping up from the shorter trips that most of his form has been over is a notable concern.

runners_data.name: Ladies Day
runners_data.note: In sharp recent form with back-to-back wins on Good ground at OR 114 and a natural desire to race prominently, but the redistribution model has placed her behind her ideal position due to the congested prominent group — she will likely need to work harder for her spot than her recent runs suggest.

runners_data.name: Norman Fletcher
runners_data.note: Consistent performer whose best form (2/17f/GOO) came close to this trip in Good going, but as a natural prominent type who has been mapped to midfield given the crowded pace picture, he will need to travel wider or later than ideal; Miss Amber Jackson-Fennell takes a 7lb claim which helps on OR 113.

runners_data.name: Buddah Castle
runners_data.note: Has an unseat in recent form and limited win data in Good conditions (2 from 4), making her the most unpredictable runner in the field; Miss Venetia Thompson (7) is a low-experience claimer and the horse's jumping reliability over hurdles is unproven at this level.

runners_data.name: Winds Of Winter
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old veteran whose natural inclination is to race prominently, yet the congested pace map means she will likely find herself shuffled back further than she would choose — her Good-ground record of 10 from 15 is solid but wins have been infrequent; style fit at 0.92 is a real concern.

runners_data.name: Heart Above
runners_data.note: Returned to winning form 20 days ago at OR 106 over a longer 21f trip on Good, which suggests this 2m1f is a little sharp, and being a natural prominent type racing out of role will blunt her chance unless the pace structure opens up gaps in the straight.

runners_data.name: Well Educated
runners_data.note: The only true hold-up runner in the field and a serial second-placer (four placed in last five on Good ground) who needs the pace to be honest to deliver a late run; George Bewley has sent out both his runners today without any 14-day winners, which is a minor flag.

races.paceDynamic: Eternal Angel is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to challenge her, Alice Stevens can dictate terms from the front at a controlled, sustainable tempo over this 2m1f Cartmel trip on Good ground. The field behind is packed with natural prominent types — Norman Fletcher, Winds Of Winter, Heart Above, and Secret Force all want to race up with the pace — but with My Chiquita, Saligo Bay, and Percy Shelley also pressing forward, there will be significant competition for the first few positions off Eternal Angel's shoulder. That cluster of prominent types jostling for position will create a busy, mid-race dynamic rather than a truly sedate gallop, meaning the pace is unlikely to be as falsely slow as a lone front-runner scenario might normally suggest. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural position; Eternal Angel is certain to lead, while My Chiquita, Percy Shelley, and Saligo Bay are best-placed to occupy the prominent slots, leaving Norman Fletcher, Winds Of Winter, and Heart Above to travel further back than they would prefer. This race shape strongly favours a well-positioned, prominent racer who can travel smoothly in the first three or four, absorb any mid-race crowding, and produce a clean jump at the last — horses forced wide or back from their natural position face a meaningful disadvantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Eternal Angel Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Eternal Angel sets a comfortable tempo unchallenged and the prominent pack settle without incident behind her.
scenarios.body: Eternal Angel dictates from the front at a measured pace on ground she handles well, and with no serious challenger able to disrupt her rhythm, she presents a stiff task for all pursuers at the business end; prominent trackers who have travelled smoothly in second or third, particularly My Chiquita and Saligo Bay, are the most dangerous threats.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pack Grinds Down Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the multiple prominent types push forward early and force a stronger gallop that eventually pegs back Eternal Angel in the straight.
scenarios.body: With several horses pressing for prominent positions the tempo proves more demanding than Eternal Angel can sustain, and she is headed approaching the last, leaving a horse who has travelled with cover just off the pace to take control; Percy Shelley, with strong Good-ground form and experience over this type of trip, and My Chiquita are the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Storm Home Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to set up a strong finishing burst for horses held up or forced wide of their natural position.
scenarios.body: Well Educated has been consistently placed without winning and would benefit from a strong pace that stretches the field, while Ladies Day — a genuine prominent type redistributed to hold-up — would need to overcome her out-of-role position, making this scenario lean heavily on Well Educated as the truest closer in the field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Fanned Wide, Chaos Decides
scenarios.trigger: If early positional jostling among the prominent cluster causes interference, disrupted jumping, or multiple horses racing far wider than ideal.
scenarios.body: Cartmel's tight, turning track punishes any horse that loses its position through traffic or jumping errors, and a runner like Buddah Castle — unpredictable in nature but capable of a clean round — could benefit from others getting into trouble; Norman Fletcher, a natural prominent type squeezed back, could also capitalise if rivals find trouble ahead of him.

watchPoints.text: Eternal Angel's ability to control tempo unchallenged is the hinge of this race — watch her jumping at the early flights, as any mistake could let the prominent cluster swamp her and change the race shape entirely.

The cluster of natural prominent runners — Norman Fletcher, Winds Of Winter, Heart Above — all seeking positions they are unlikely to secure creates a real risk of early crowding or interference on Cartmel's tight early bends; watch the first two furlongs carefully.

Saligo Bay has not run for 168 days and all five recent runs were on softer ground than today's Good; if she shows any sign of needing the run or failing to handle the going, her prominent position could become a liability for runners around her.

Well Educated is the only genuine closer in the field — if she is seen making unusually strong late ground, it is a sign the pace has been genuinely demanding and the prominent racers in front may be vulnerable to a fast finisher at the line.

Percy Shelley's visor is noted — headgear changes at Cartmel on Good ground can sharpen a horse's jumping focus, and with 14 from 15 in similar conditions, any market support late should be taken seriously as a tactical signal.

races.name: Cartmel Crystal Cup Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Tommie Beau
runners_data.note: Hold-up profile ideally suited to waiting tactics; veteran of 11 who has won and placed repeatedly at 28-30f on Good ground, and a recent course form entry is encouraging — Benjamin Macey's 5lb claim is a live bonus at the weights over this Cartmel test|

runners_data.name: Peaky Boy
runners_data.note: Trainer Jonjo O'Neill in cracking current form (4/14 over 14 days) and the tongue-tie is noted; as the sole front-runner he controls his own destiny, but his style-fit tag (0.91) reflects that he is racing at the sharp end of his comfort zone in this prominently-loaded field|

runners_data.name: Homme Public
runners_data.note: Jack Tudor takes over for Greenall/Guerriero, who have had two winners in the last eight days; hold-up in style and has placed at 18f on Good, so the step back to a genuine 2m6f Cartmel test should not be an issue — tongue-tie and pads retained|

runners_data.name: Caughtinyourtrance
runners_data.note: Brian Hughes aboard a horse in strong form (win-win-second from last three), clearly thrives on Good ground at distances around 2m6f, and has placed twice at this sort of trip in similar conditions — the prominent style he carries is genuine and he is one of the few who can credibly secure that position|

runners_data.name: Shantwopointfive
runners_data.note: 196-day absence is the overriding concern here; Sam England's horse showed a win on soft and a placed effort on Good in his history but the long layoff and a P-P-5-2-P recent form string suggest he could need this sharply — prominent style but likely to sit off the pace after a long break|

runners_data.name: Howdoyalikeherhome
runners_data.note: Sent to Gordon Elliott's yard, quick turnaround (12 days), and has fallen at the last fence in his most recent run — P-P-F recent form and only one win from 11 Good-ground starts makes him awkward to trust, though tongue-tie and bar are worn|

runners_data.name: High Dancer
runners_data.note: Nicky Richards has him in good form (1-2 from last five), recently won and placed at 16-20f on Good ground, and Danny McMenamin is a confident booking; prominently-run and genuine, 6-year-old is the youngest horse in the field with upside, but a step up to 2m6f is uncharted territory|

runners_data.name: Oakley
runners_data.note: Three wins and nine places from 15 Good-ground starts underlines his affinity for this going; in reality a front-running type who will be squeezed out of that position by the prominent logjam — Conor Ring will need to find cover rather than the leading berth Oakley prefers|

runners_data.name: Roaring Home
runners_data.note: Sam Twiston-Davies picks up this consistent horse who has won at 20-24f on Good and has a fine 10/15 record in similar conditions; though mapped to midfield by redistribution, his natural energy will be spent getting to the front — if he gets the position he craves the form is solid|

runners_data.name: Dinons
runners_data.note: Aged 13 but still places at 24f on Good ground with regularity; hold-up type for Brian Ellison, Nathan Moscrop takes the ride, and his consistency (no win recently but always in the frame) makes him a quiet each-way participant if the race plays to a patient profile|

runners_data.name: Belles Benefit
runners_data.note: Won latest over 22f on Good and clearly a consistent performer (two wins from nine recent Good-ground starts); an enthusiastic front-to-mid type by nature who will be squeezed inward by the prominent cluster — Harry Bannister may find clean air if he drops out rather than fighting for position|

runners_data.name: Evenwood Sonofagun
runners_data.note: Lizzie Quinlan runner with Gavin Sheehan aboard; won over 22f on Good and placed at 26f, so the trip is within range — a natural prominent mover who, along with stablemate Rauzan, will find this competitive positional environment difficult, tongue-tie and pads worn|

runners_data.name: Rauzan
runners_data.note: Stable companion of Evenwood Sonofagun and hold-up by style; Sean Quinlan aboard, but the form record shows no win or place in the last five Good-ground appearances (0W0P) which is a damning statistic — the visor is noted but the evidence for improvement is thin|

races.paceDynamic: Peaky Boy is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 13-runner field, and with no serious rival willing or likely able to push him from the front over 2m6f at Cartmel, he sets a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset — this is not a searching pace but a steady one that keeps the race together until the home turn. The field contains a heavy overload of prominent-profile horses: Oakley, Roaring Home, Belles Benefit, Evenwood Sonofagun, Caughtinyourtrance, Shantwopointfive, High Dancer, and Howdoyalikeherhome all want to race prominently, meaning several will be forced to race wider or further back than their natural inclination, burning energy fighting for position in the first mile. This compression of prominent types behind a single unhurried leader creates an unusually congested midfield and a race likely run at a tempo that does not fully test stamina, leaving a late sprint premium. The tactical verdict is clear: hold-up horses who can travel wide of the scrimmage and deliver a sustained late run — particularly those with proven Good-ground form at this sort of distance — are best placed to exploit the positional chaos ahead of them.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Peaky Boy dictates an uncontested, measured tempo and the prominent cluster traffic-jams behind him
scenarios.body: Peaky Boy controls at a comfortable clip, leaving little energy expenditure up front, while the press of prominent types jostle for position in the pack; at the home turn the gaps open and hold-up horses with a clean run produce the strongest finishes

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Cut Loose
scenarios.trigger: If Caughtinyourtrance and High Dancer manage to break clear of the prominent logjam and race just off Peaky Boy in a clear first two
scenarios.body: The early order settles into a manageable rhythm for those who actually secure the handy positions, and horses racing with cover in the first three or four are rewarded as the race develops naturally without the midfield scramble

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Stays
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is so generous that Peaky Boy or a horse who slides into a prominent slot simply outstays a field that has used energy scrapping for position
scenarios.body: The race pans out as a test of position-holding rather than a finish, with the horse who avoids the midfield squeeze and travels sweetly close to the pace proving impossible to peg back over the final two flights

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Produces Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent logjam causes interference or a messy mid-race reshuffle that disrupts most fancied runners
scenarios.body: A lightly-weighted or unconsidered rival who finds an unexpected passage or benefits from the carnage in the pack runs through beaten horses to claim an unlikely placing

watchPoints.text: Prominent overload — Oakley, Roaring Home, Belles Benefit, and Evenwood Sonofagun all want to race positively but cannot all get their natural position; watch for early crowding and interference on the first circuit at Cartmel's tight bends.

Tommie Beau has won over 29-30f on Good at Cartmel in recent history and Benjamin Macey's 5lb claim reduces his weight meaningfully — if the race is run at the predicted steady pace, his late run from off it could be decisive.

Shantwopointfive returns from 196 days off and has a recent record of pulled-up runs; watch for any early signs of reluctance or lack of fluency that could compromise the safety of the field at the jumps.

High Dancer steps up significantly in trip to 2m6f for the first time — if the pace quickens earlier than expected on this Cartmel circuit, his stamina question is an unresolved factor that could see him fade when it matters.

Peaky Boy holds the tempo key: if Jonjo O'Neill Jr. allows him to bowl along unchallenged, the whole pace map hinges on whether that gallop is truly steady or deceptively quick — monitor the early fractions relative to Cartmel's 2m6f standard.

races.name: Sun Racing Summer Jumps Championship Handicap Steeple Chase

runners_data.name: Roxboro River
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer with a solid base of Good-ground form, consistent if rarely winning, and 15/15 similar-going entries back his current conditions; Harry Atkins (5lb claimer) takes off useful weight but ask is whether a steady pace gives him enough to close from the rear.

runners_data.name: Jeteye
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner who has won and placed repeatedly at 24f on Good; Sam England has a runner in recent form (1/6 T14) and the horse's tongue-tie and prominent style suits a race where he can dictate; the STYLE_FIT flag (0.92) is benign here as he IS racing in his role.

runners_data.name: Halfway House Lad
runners_data.note: Won two of his last three completed starts on Good ground at 24-26f for James Moffatt, form 66-11P is mixed but the wins are recent and significant; Brian Hughes is a major booking and the horse's prominent style suits a race run at a controlled front-running pace; limited similar-going data (6/15) is the only caveat.

runners_data.name: Wearelongterm
runners_data.note: 153-day absence is a significant flag for this hold-up horse whose entire form base is on Soft ground (4 of 5 recent runs); Danny McMenamin keeps the ride but the lack of recent activity combined with a going preference mismatch makes this a risky proposition, however cheap the price.

runners_data.name: Star Turn
runners_data.note: Consistent placer on Good ground at staying trips (three seconds in Good-ground chases), though yet to win over fences; Mr J P Murray (7lb claimer) lightens the load and the horse's hold-up style is genuine, but he requires enough pace to produce his effort late and this is not guaranteed here.

runners_data.name: Lights Are Green
runners_data.note: Prominent-style nine-year-old whose form string (4PP-3P) suggests jumping is a concern — three pulls-up in five recent runs is alarming in a 3m1½f chase; Jonathon Bewley is an able pilot but 42 days off and that completion rate must be respected before giving weight to any positional advantage.

runners_data.name: Kingofthegame
runners_data.note: Won two of his last three completed starts at 26f on Good ground for Martin Todhunter, making him one of the in-form prominent types in the field; Ryan Mania is an experienced northern jockey who suits the track, and the horse's jumping record over these distances looks reliable.

runners_data.name: Tell Me Again
runners_data.note: Carries a true hold-up profile but is pushed into a midfield mapping because the field is stacked with deep closers; his own recent form (3-U485) is modest and he has not placed in five straight attempts, so even if he finds his natural berth late, the form does not strongly suggest he will capitalise.

runners_data.name: Judicial Review
runners_data.note: A genuine prominent type whose last six entries include significant beaten distances — form 9P-67P tells a story of a horse struggling to compete at this level; carrying a STYLE_FIT discount (0.93) because he is mapped to midfield against his nature, and Leah Noreci's 7lb claim offers slim compensation for the form concerns.

runners_data.name: Dreamings Free
runners_data.note: Carries an explicit fade-in-finish flag which is deeply problematic for a hold-up horse over 3m1½f; Daniel Bourne sends him out just 16 days after his last run and his recent form (2380-9) shows sharp deterioration — mapped to midfield against his natural rear-of-field style, the combination of fade risk and positional dislocation makes him very difficult to recommend.

races.paceDynamic: Jeteye is the sole confirmed front-runner in this field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should be allowed to bowl along at a sustainable, self-set tempo over the 3m1½f trip on Good ground at Cartmel. Halfway House Lad, Lights Are Green, and Kingofthegame are all prominent-style horses who will push forward behind Jeteye, creating a compact early order but not a true pace battle. The field contains more hold-up and prominent types than the map can accommodate naturally — Judicial Review (true prominent), Tell Me Again, and Dreamings Free (true hold-up horses) are all likely to be squeezed into midfield positions that are not their preferred role. With an uncontested front-runner setting a measured gallop over a stiff distance, this race shape is likely to play into the hands of prominent-to-midfield horses with stamina and a turn of foot in the final stages, rather than deep closers who need a truly honest pace to exploit.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Jeteye Controls, Stamina Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Jeteye dictates an uncontested, even gallop and the prominent pack is unable to reel him in before the last, stamina-rich prominent runners finish strongest.
scenarios.body: Jeteye's recorded wins at 24f on Good suggest he handles this trip and surface, and a solo lead at a steady tempo means his jumping efficiency becomes a key weapon over 3m1½f; horses who travel prominently and stay every yard will overhaul any who fade.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Strike Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens mid-race and the prominent pack burns off early, leaving enough of a true run for closers to pick up from off the gallop.
scenarios.body: Roxboro River is the most authentic hold-up performer in the field with consistent form on Good ground and experience at this sort of trip, and if the pace genuinely tests the leaders on the final circuit he is ideally placed to pass tired rivals.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Pair Clear
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners push forward and establish a breakaway group that is never seriously challenged by the hold-up horses in the final mile.
scenarios.body: Jeteye and Halfway House Lad both carry positive recent form at this sort of distance on Good, and if the closers — several of whom are racing out of their natural role — cannot close the gap in the straight, the front two may finish well clear.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Midfield Types Profit
scenarios.trigger: If early jumping errors or a field-wide mid-race surge disrupts the order, leaving a horse from the reshuffled midfield to profit from a muddling finish.
scenarios.body: With Judicial Review, Tell Me Again, and Dreamings Free all forced into midfield positions against their natural style, any positional scramble could flatter a horse who finds clear daylight at a crucial moment; however, Dreamings Free carries a fade warning and Tell Me Again has a modest recent profile, limiting this scenario's value.

watchPoints.text: Lights Are Green has pulled up in three of his last five starts — watch for early jumping errors or a refusal signal at the first, as a stricken runner at pace over fences in a 10-horse field is a material safety and race-shape risk.

Wearelongterm returns from 153 days off on going that is firmer than his entire recent form base (all Soft); if he shows signs of reluctance or movement irregularity in the parade ring or early stages, his hold-up role means he could be a late-race hazard rather than a contender.

Dreamings Free is flagged as a horse who fades in the finish — over 3m1½f with a hold-up style forced into midfield, watch for him stopping abruptly in the final mile and potentially causing interference to horses challenging from behind.

Kingofthegame and Halfway House Lad are both prominent types with recent winning form on Good ground; if either breaks sharply and sits directly behind Jeteye from the first fence, they become dangerous as the front-running tempo is unlikely to be truly searching enough to stop them.

Roxboro River's jockey, 5lb claimer Harry Atkins, is worth monitoring through the early stages — if he positions the horse too far back in a field where the hold-up role may not be rewarded at a steady pace, the gap may simply be too large to bridge in the closing stages at Cartmel.

races.name: Shorefield Supplies Handicap Steeple Chase

runners_data.name: Cuzco Du Mathan
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse who has finished no better than fourth at this trip on Good ground in recent runs (sim-going 0W0P over 15f), with the 7lb claimer Leah Noreci adding further risk; 52 days off the track and blinkers applied, so pace positioning at the rear looks set again.

runners_data.name: Dexter
runners_data.note: Trainer Greenall/Guerriero in decent 14-day form (2/8) and Toby Wynne takes over; strong Good-ground record (sim-going 1W7P/13 runs) and at 9 has the class and experience to slot in behind Blazing Court and utilise his prominent tendency even in a compressed field.

runners_data.name: Forsa Bay
runners_data.note: Longest absence in the field at 71 days and a visor fitted — a true hold-up horse whose last run ended in a pull-up (P); his natural style will be to sit last, but with so many hold-up types here his position in the bunch is unavoidable rather than chosen, and the fitness question after 10 weeks off is real.

runners_data.name: Clean Getaway
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's yard 2/18 in 14 days and the horse has course-relevant Good-ground form (1W5P/13), most recently finishing 3rd and 5th; naturally wants to come from behind but wears a plain hood and holds genuine each-way claims if tucked in mid-division — the style compromise is a factor.

runners_data.name: Cawthorne Cracker
runners_data.note: Consistent without winning — five placings in last five starts, all on Good or similar — and Jack Tudor is a high-quality booking from the Greenall/Guerriero yard; the horse's true closer style is squeezed by the pack here, but the jumping record (tp headgear) is solid and he stays in range if the pace weakens.

runners_data.name: Blazing Court
runners_data.note: The one horse guaranteed its preferred front-running position; form string 05U-UP is full of non-completions and the trainer-ridden amateur (Mr John Dixon, 7lb claim) is an unknown quantity, yet solo leadership on Good ground at Cartmel is a significant tactical gift — his chance hinges entirely on jumping cleanly and controlling tempo.

runners_data.name: Out On Her Own
runners_data.note: Lightly weighted at OR 76, Ryan Mania is a strong jockey booking for Dianne Sayer; the mare has Good-ground form (0W2P/9 sim-going) and showed a 2nd recently, but her genuine hold-up style means she will be further from the pace than ideal, and no headgear fitted suggests no change of approach.

runners_data.name: Getaway Jewel
runners_data.note: Aged 12 and returning quickly (11 days) for Micky Hammond and Brian Hughes — the most experienced jockey in the field; consistent on Good ground (1W7P/12) and placed second last time, but advanced age and a true staying-on style from the rear make her dependent on others making mistakes rather than winning through pace.

races.paceDynamic: Blazing Court is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner field and, as the only horse willing to lead, will set a solo, uncontested gallop from the front over 2m1½f on Good ground at Cartmel. With no rival likely to challenge for the lead, Blazing Court's trainer-ridden amateur combination (Mr John Dixon) will be able to control tempo entirely, choosing a measured, sustainable pace that keeps the race honest without burning the horse up. That scenario strongly favours horses with tactical speed who can travel close to the pace and pounce from a prominent position, rather than pure closers who need a true gallop to close the gap. The field holds markedly more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate — Forsa Bay, Clean Getaway, Cawthorne Cracker, Out On Her Own and Getaway Jewel are all genuine rear-of-field horses mapped to midfield on the diagram because there simply is no room for them all to race in their natural position; only Blazing Court is certain to get its preferred berth, with Dexter and Cuzco Du Mathan best-placed to creep into a prominent role behind it.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Blazing Court Controls Serenely
scenarios.trigger: If Blazing Court dictates an uncontested, measured tempo and the closers cannot bridge the gap from midfield on Good ground.
scenarios.body: Blazing Court bowls along in front at a comfortable clip, the amateur rider keeping it relaxed over the fences while the pack of hold-up horses are left with too much to do on a track that does not easily yield late ground; horses who can travel in second or third without getting outpaced early are best placed to challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is deceptively strong early and the closers get a genuine gallop to aim at in the straight.
scenarios.body: A stronger-than-expected tempo — perhaps if the amateur on Blazing Court finds it hard to rate accurately — strings the field out and leaves genuine hold-up types with enough pace to reel in the leader; Good ground at Cartmel suits those coming from off the pace if the fractions are honest.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Duel Home
scenarios.trigger: If a second horse pushes Blazing Court into a faster pace than intended and the race develops into a two-horse battle early.
scenarios.body: Should any rider on a redistributed horse decide to force their natural prominent position, the race tempo lifts and the winner emerges from those who can handle a contested early pace and still jump cleanly down the back; this shape suits a horse with both stamina and jumping accuracy.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Attrition Chaos Decides
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or fallers disrupt the race pattern and reduce the field late, leaving survivors rather than tactical winners.
scenarios.body: With several horses rated below OR 90 and a field containing error-prone profiles across 15 fences, the race could lose key protagonists and become a test of jumping soundness rather than pace shape; any horse that jumps cleanly and is placed within reach of the front can inherit a winning position.

watchPoints.text: Blazing Court jumping — if Mr John Dixon's amateur ride puts in a bad jump at an early fence and loses the lead, the entire race shape collapses and a scramble for position begins.
Forsa Bay fitness — 71 days off the track with a visor fitted; if the layoff has left him short, he will drop out quickly and could interfere with trailing horses on the tight Cartmel circuit.

Getaway Jewel's age (12) means she is statistically more likely to make a jumping error under pressure late; Brian Hughes will be aware, but watch whether she loses her action on the run to the second-last.
Dexter's hood (tp) — if the headgear has its intended effect and he travels prominently behind Blazing Court, he becomes the most likely horse to inherit the lead if the front-runner makes a mistake.

Pack congestion on first circuit — with five genuine hold-up horses all forced into a compressed midfield group, watch for crowding and shuffling at early fences where Cartmel's tight turns compress the field sharply.

races.name: Charnley's Home & Garden Centre Handicap Steeple Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Red Happy
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins over this trip on Good ground gives him a strong profile for today; front-running style suits Cartmel's turning track ideally, and Jonathon Bewley is stable jockey for the Bewley operation who fired a blank in the last 14 days, but the horse's form speaks for itself — the slight style-fit flag is minimal given he is the confirmed leader.

runners_data.name: Lermoos Legend
runners_data.note: Mickey Bowen's stable had a runner in the last 14 days (0 from 8, a concern for form students), and at 11 years old this veteran needs things to go right; he is a natural prominent racer who should secure second or third early, and his two most recent wins came over 20f on Good ground, making the step up in trip a mild query.

runners_data.name: Passengerontheship
runners_data.note: Five consecutive wins is an outstanding recent record and Sam England's yard posted a winner in the last 14 days; however, his natural front-running instincts are genuinely compromised here — the map forces him into a midfield berth he won't want, and his chances hinge on whether he can settle when denied his usual position rather than burning energy fighting for the front.

runners_data.name: Got Grey
runners_data.note: Leah Noreci claims 7lbs which lowers his effective weight meaningfully, and his going record at 13 from 15 sim-going runs shows he handles Good reliably; a true hold-up horse who will be produced from the rear, he needs the pace to be strong enough to soften the principals and Cartmel's brevity of straight is a real obstacle to his style.

runners_data.name: Sean Og
runners_data.note: Sean Quinlan, a shrewd jumps jockey, partners a horse who won last time out over the same course and distance — that course-and-distance form is significant; like Passengerontheship, his prominent nature is squeezed out by this field shape, and his effectiveness today depends largely on whether Quinlan can find him a good position without costing ground early.

runners_data.name: Moodofthemoment
runners_data.note: Lilly Pinchin rides at a useful claim and David Thompson's runner arrives on a very short 16-day turnaround; the horse's headgear note (previously ran in a hood/p) and a form string showing several pulled-up or non-completions raises jumping reliability questions, and as a genuine hold-up type he faces the same Cartmel straight problem as Got Grey but with less compelling form behind him.

races.paceDynamic: Red Happy is the confirmed front-runner and will likely dictate from the front at Cartmel, a track where controlling the pace from an early stage is a significant advantage given its sharp, turning nature. With Passengerontheship and Sean Og both natural prominent types redistributed to midfield slots because the front positions are already congested, the pace should be honest but not suicidal — Red Happy sets a sustainable tempo without serious pressure from behind. Lermoos Legend will also push forward and compete for the early prominent positions, meaning the front two will establish the race's rhythm, leaving the genuine hold-up horses Got Grey and Moodofthemoment with ground to make up from the rear. This race shape most favours runners able to track the leader in second or third without expending energy fighting for position — a contested but controlled pace with a single clear front-runner on a tight track points squarely at a held-up prominent finisher who can deliver a sustained gallop rather than a flat-out sprint. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural position; Red Happy is best placed to lead, with Lermoos Legend most likely to lock in second, while Passengerontheship and Sean Og face the biggest compromise of their running styles.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Red Happy Controls, Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Red Happy dictates an uncontested or lightly-pressured gallop and the prominent trackers fail to mount a sustained challenge from the final fence.
scenarios.body: Red Happy, proven front-runner at 9 with back-to-back wins over similar Good ground and trip, uses Cartmel's tight bends to bottleneck chasers and maintain his advantage into the straight; the sustainable pace means he conserves enough energy to repel challengers late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Overhauels Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Lermoos Legend or a true prominent type sits a length or two off the pace and produces a clean round of jumping to collar Red Happy after the last.
scenarios.body: The lead changes hands in the closing stages as the tracker benefits from a stronger finishing position and avoids the energy cost of front-running; Cartmel's run-in rewards horses who travel sweetly just off the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to string out the field and a hold-up horse produces a sustained late run to pick off tired front-runners.
scenarios.body: Got Grey or Moodofthemoment, settled at the rear, finds the principals tiring over the final fences and delivers a relentless staying finish; however, Cartmel's tight track and limited straight make this genuinely hard to execute from far back.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Red Happy weakens abruptly or makes a critical jumping error mid-race, causing a scramble for the lead and a messy tactical race.
scenarios.body: Redistributed prominents Passengerontheship and Sean Og, unable to get their natural position early, benefit if the race suddenly opens up and they can assert; Sean Og's recent course form makes him a live danger in a reshuffled scenario.

watchPoints.text: Watch Red Happy's jumping closely — if he makes an early error the entire race shape unravels, because no other runner is positioned or primed to take up the running cleanly given the redistribution of prominent types.
Passengerontheship's behaviour in the first half-mile is key — if he fights for a lead position he can't have, the energy cost could compromise a horse with otherwise outstanding recent form.
Lermoos Legend's trainer has gone 0 from 8 in the past 14 days; at age 11, any sign of a flat-topped market drift should be noted as a possible indicator of stable form concerns.

Got Grey's 7lb claimer Leah Noreci makes him notably lighter than his rivals on adjusted weights — if the pace is truly end-to-end, monitor whether he creeps into contention approaching the second-last earlier than his odds suggest.

Moodofthemoment's string of pulled-up runs (two P's in recent form) makes watching his early jumping particularly relevant — any fence-related scratchiness early could signal another non-completion before the race develops.
